title: "Time spent travelling to the disposal site during pit emptying jobs in Mzuzu, Malawi"
author:
  - name: Padraic Casserly
    email: pcasserly@ethz.ch
    affiliations:
      - name: Global Health Engineering, ETH Zürich
date: 2026-09-29
bibliography: references.bib
abstract: |
  We use task-level timing data recorded with the Gulper Timer app during
  ridealong observations of manual pit latrine emptying in Mzuzu, Malawi, to
  quantify how much time a pit emptying team spends travelling to the sludge
  disposal site, for the jobs in which such a trip was made. Travel time is
  reported per job in two ways: elapsed time (clock hours during which the
  team was on a trip, with simultaneous travel by several workers counted
  once) and labour time (person-hours, the sum of every worker's recorded
  travel).
---

```{.r .cell-code .hidden}
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(knitr)

tasks <- read_csv("../../data/all_tasks.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

fmt <- function(x, digits = 1) format(round(x, digits), nsmall = digits, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE)

n_jobs_all <- n_distinct(tasks$job_id)
n_entries <- nrow(tasks)
n_workers <- n_distinct(tasks$gulper_id)
dates <- as.Date(substr(unique(tasks$job_id), 1, 10))
total_labour_h <- sum(tasks$duration_seconds) / 3600

job_labour <- tasks |>
  group_by(job_id) |>
  summarise(job_labour_h = sum(duration_seconds) / 3600, .groups = "drop")

# Errands, excluded from the analysis but described in Methods
errands <- tasks |> filter(task == "Travel", subtask == "On errand")

# Disposal-site travel entries, with overlapping entries within a job merged
# into trips: an entry starts a new trip if it begins after every earlier
# entry of the job has ended.
min_trip_min <- 5

travel <- tasks |>
  filter(task == "Travel", subtask == "Travel to disposal site") |>
  mutate(s = as.numeric(entry_start_time), e = as.numeric(entry_end_time)) |>
  arrange(job_id, s) |>
  group_by(job_id) |>
  mutate(prev_end = lag(cummax(e), default = -Inf), trip = cumsum(s > prev_end)) |>
  ungroup()

trips_all <- travel |>
  group_by(job_id, trip) |>
  summarise(
    start = min(s), end = max(e),
    gulpers = n_distinct(gulper_id),
    entries = n(),
    labour_h = sum(duration_seconds) / 3600,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(clock_min = (end - start) / 60, keep = clock_min >= min_trip_min)

trips <- trips_all |> filter(keep)
short <- trips_all |> filter(!keep)

summarise_jobs <- function(tr) {
  tr |>
    group_by(job_id) |>
    summarise(
      date = as.Date(substr(first(job_id), 1, 10)),
      trips = n(),
      gulpers = max(gulpers),
      clock_h = sum(end - start) / 3600,
      labour_h = sum(labour_h),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    left_join(job_labour, by = "job_id") |>
    mutate(share = 100 * labour_h / job_labour_h)
}

jobs <- summarise_jobs(trips)
jobs_unfiltered <- summarise_jobs(trips_all)

n_travel_jobs <- nrow(jobs)
n_trips <- nrow(trips)
mean_clock_h <- mean(jobs$clock_h)
median_clock_h <- median(jobs$clock_h)
mean_labour_h <- mean(jobs$labour_h)
median_labour_h <- median(jobs$labour_h)
mean_trip_min <- mean(trips$clock_min)
mean_gulpers_trip <- mean(trips$gulpers)
ratio <- sum(jobs$labour_h) / sum(jobs$clock_h)
travel_share_total <- 100 * sum(jobs$labour_h) / total_labour_h

# Recording sessions (data review): does any travel job hold two sessions?
sessions <- tasks |>
  group_by(job_id) |>
  summarise(n_sessions = sum(entry_number == 1), .groups = "drop")
split_travel_jobs <- sessions |>
  filter(n_sessions > 1, job_id %in% jobs$job_id) |>
  pull(job_id)
```

# Introduction

Time-driven activity-based costing (TDABC) allocates costs to activities based
on the time resources spend on them. Manual pit emptying in Mzuzu involves not
only emptying the pit but also transporting the extracted sludge to a disposal
site, an activity that takes the whole team away from the site and consumes
labour capacity that must be costed. This short manuscript answers the
question: **What is the average time spent per job travelling to the disposal
site, when a team travels to the disposal site?**

# Data and methods

The dataset (`data/all_tasks.csv`) contains 10,784 task entries
recorded for 36 pit emptying jobs between
08 May 2026 and 14 September 2026,
performed by 19 anonymised pit emptiers ("gulpers"). Each entry
records one worker performing one task with a start time, end time and
duration in seconds. The Travel task has two subtasks: *On errand*, for short
in-job errands, and *Travel to disposal site*, for transporting sludge away
from the site. Only the second is analysed here. The
106 errand entries (15.5
person-hours in 22 jobs) are excluded. Travel
from the gulpers' base to the job site is not among the recorded tasks, so
the figures below cover disposal trips made during a job only.

Gulpers travel to the disposal site together, so each trip appears in the data
as several near-identical entries, one per worker. Within each job, entries
that overlap in time are merged into a single **trip** running from the
earliest start to the latest end. Travel time per job is then reported in two
ways:

- **Elapsed time (clock hours):** the summed duration of the job's trips. A
  trip made by four gulpers together counts once. This is the headline
  measure, since it answers how long the team was away.
- **Labour time (person-hours):** the sum of `duration_seconds` over all
  disposal-site entries, i.e. every worker's travel added together. This is
  the measure relevant for TDABC, where labour capacity is the resource being
  costed, and it matches the measure used in the companion manuscript on
  total job time.

The population is the set of jobs in which the team travelled to the disposal
site. Genuine trips last 28–46
minutes. A few disposal-site entries are far shorter and cannot represent a
trip: 3 merged intervals of under 5 minutes
(3, 42, 69 seconds), each
recorded by one or two workers and including a 2.9-second entry already
flagged in the data review. These are treated as accidental taps and dropped,
which removes 3.0 person-minutes. One job
(2026-09-03_03) has only such an entry and
therefore does not count as a job with a disposal trip. The effect of keeping
these entries is reported in the Results.

Other data checks: the file has no missing values except `subtask`, which is
empty by design for the Rest and Disposal tasks. Recorded durations agree with
the difference between end and start times to within ±1 second. No job crosses
midnight, so elapsed time can be computed from clock times directly.

# Results

A team travelled to the disposal site in **7 of the
36 observed jobs**, making 11 trips in total. In those
jobs, the team spent on average **0.9 clock hours
(52 minutes) per job travelling to the disposal
site** (median 0.6 hours, range
0.5–1.7). In labour time this is
3.0 person-hours per job (median 2.2,
range 0.9–6.0).

A job with a disposal trip had 1.6 trips on average,
each lasting 33 minutes and made by
3.4 gulpers together, so labour time is
3.4 times elapsed time. Within these jobs, disposal travel took up
17 % of the job's labour time on average
(range 9–24 %). Across all
36 jobs, disposal travel accounts for
4.1 % of the 509.0 person-hours
recorded. @tbl-jobs lists each job and @fig-jobs shows the elapsed travel time
per job.


::: {#tbl-jobs .cell tbl-cap='Disposal-site travel for each job in which a trip was made. Elapsed time counts a trip once regardless of how many gulpers made it; labour time adds every gulper\'s travel. Share is labour travel time as a percentage of the job\'s total labour time.'}

```{.r .cell-code .hidden}
jobs |>
  transmute(
    Job = job_id,
    Trips = as.character(trips),
    Gulpers = as.character(gulpers),
    `Elapsed (h)` = clock_h,
    `Labour (person-h)` = labour_h,
    `Share of job (%)` = share
  ) |>
  bind_rows(tibble(
    Job = "Mean", Trips = fmt(mean(jobs$trips)), Gulpers = fmt(mean(jobs$gulpers)),
    `Elapsed (h)` = mean_clock_h, `Labour (person-h)` = mean_labour_h,
    `Share of job (%)` = mean(jobs$share)
  )) |>
  kable(digits = 1, align = "lrrrrr")
```

![Elapsed time spent travelling to the disposal site per job, for the jobs in which a trip was made, ordered by date. Labels give the number of trips. The dashed line is the mean.](index_files/figure-docx/fig-jobs-1.png){#fig-jobs}

:::


Travel time per job is driven mainly by the number of trips: jobs with one
trip take about half an hour of elapsed time, and the two jobs with the most
travel (2026-08-08_01 and 2026-09-08_01)
made 3 and 2
trips respectively.

Two sensitivity checks. First, keeping the short entries dropped in the
Methods adds one job and changes the mean elapsed travel time to
0.8 hours over
8 jobs (2.6
person-hours); this is lower only because the added job contributes a
0.7-minute entry. Second, the data
review found three job IDs that each hold two recording sessions by different
crews and may be two jobs. None of the jobs with a disposal trip is among them, so the result is unaffected.

# Conclusion

When a pit emptying team in Mzuzu travels to the disposal site, it spends on
average **0.9 clock hours (52
minutes) per job** on that travel, corresponding to
**3.0 person-hours** of labour because
3.4 gulpers travel together. A single trip takes about
33 minutes, and jobs vary mainly in how many trips they
need. Such trips occurred in 7 of the 36 observed
jobs. For TDABC purposes the person-hour figure is the quantity to cost, and
it should be applied only to jobs that require a disposal trip.

# Appendix A: Relevant literature {.appendix}

The five references in the author's Zotero library most relevant to this
analysis, with one sentence on why each matters here:

1. @yesaya2021cost apply time-driven activity-based costing to compost
   production in Blantyre, Malawi, making it the closest methodological
   precedent for turning the per-job travel times measured here into an
   activity cost.
2. @wilcox2026formal analyse the costs of 23 formal manual emptying providers
   in Malawi and Uganda and find labour is what makes manual emptying
   expensive, which is why the person-hours that a team spends travelling to
   the disposal site are a key costing input.
3. @chipeta2017designing designed and tested the pedal-powered Gulper pump in
   Mzuzu and estimated a pit can be emptied in 1–2 hours when trash content
   is low, so a half-hour disposal trip is a substantial addition to a job.
4. @chiposa2017characterization characterise pit latrines in peri-urban
   Mzuzu, reporting that 90 % of households also dispose of domestic waste
   in their pits, which affects how much material must be removed and hence
   how many disposal trips a job needs.
5. @burt2019costs estimate the cost of delivering pit emptying services in
   Kigali, Rwanda, at different scales, giving a comparison point for costs
   derived from the travel times reported here.
